expected_core_reactions.description: LpxA acylates UDP-GlcNAc using a FAS II-derived beta-hydroxyacyl-ACP donor; the paper states the reaction is reversible and thermodynamically unfavourable
products: acylated UDP-GlcNAc (referred to only as 'the LpxA product'; not chemically named in this paper's body)
expected_core_reactions.quote: The first enzyme in the Raetz pathway, LpxA, acylates uridine diphosphate- N -acetyl-glucosamine (UDP-GlcNAc) using a β-hydroxyacyl-acyl carrier protein (ACP) substrate made by the type II fatty acid synthesis pathway (FAS II)
expected_core_reactions.rationale: The paper names it as the first enzymatic step of the Raetz pathway with an explicit acyl acceptor and an explicit acyl donor.

expected_core_reactions.description: LpxC deacetylates the LpxA product, removing the acetyl group from the GlcNAc moiety; the first irreversible and committed step of lipid A biosynthesis
products: deacetylated LpxA product (not chemically named for E. coli in this paper)
expected_core_reactions.quote: LpxC is a deacetylase that removes the acetyl group from the GlcNAc moiety to allow for the addition of the next acyl group by LpxD and subsequent removal of UMP by LpxH, LpxI, or LpxG depending on the organism
expected_core_reactions.rationale: The paper explicitly asserts the chemical transformation (deacetylation of the GlcNAc moiety) and designates it the committed step of the requested pathway.

expected_core_reactions.description: LpxD adds the next acyl group to the deacetylated LpxC product
substrates: deacetylated LpxC product (not chemically named in this paper)
products: further acylated UDP-glucosamine species (not chemically named in this paper)
expected_core_reactions.quote: to allow for the addition of the next acyl group by LpxD
expected_core_reactions.rationale: The paper asserts the transformation type (addition of the next acyl group) and the catalyst, but names neither substrate nor product as a chemical species.

expected_core_reactions.description: LpxH (or LpxI or LpxG, depending on the organism) removes UMP from the LpxD product
substrates: LpxD product (not chemically named in this paper)
products: de-UMP-ylated monosaccharide lipid A precursor (not chemically named in this paper)
expected_core_reactions.quote: subsequent removal of UMP by LpxH, LpxI, or LpxG depending on the organism
expected_core_reactions.rationale: The paper asserts the transformation and names UMP as the leaving product, but does not pin which of the three paralogues acts in E. coli and does not name the lipid substrate.

expected_core_reactions.description: LpxB condenses two monosaccharide precursors to form a tetra-acylated disaccharide intermediate
substrates: monosaccharide lipid A precursors (not individually named in this paper)
expected_core_reactions.quote: LpxB then catalyzes the formation of a tetra-acylated disaccharide intermediate
expected_core_reactions.rationale: The paper asserts the catalyst and names the product explicitly; this is the disaccharide-forming step of the requested pathway.

expected_core_reactions.description: LpxK phosphorylates the tetra-acylated disaccharide intermediate to produce lipid IVA
expected_core_reactions.quote: LpxB then catalyzes the formation of a tetra-acylated disaccharide intermediate, which is phosphorylated by LpxK to produce lipid IV A
expected_core_reactions.rationale: Substrate, product and catalyst are all asserted in one clause of the pathway paragraph.

expected_core_reactions.description: WaaA transfers Kdo residue(s) onto lipid IVA to form Kdo-lipid IVA (the first sugar(s) of the core)
expected_core_reactions.quote: Next, WaaA adds a number of Kdo residues that depends on the organism to form the first sugar(s) of the core, resulting in Kdo-lipid IV A
expected_core_reactions.rationale: Explicit substrate-to-product conversion with a named catalyst; the paper places it inside the Kdo-lipid A biosynthesis pathway of Figure 1B.

expected_core_reactions.description: LpxL performs the first of two sequential acylations of Kdo-lipid IVA
products: singly acylated Kdo-lipid IVA intermediate (not named in this paper)
expected_core_reactions.quote: Kdo-lipid IV A which is sequentially acylated by LpxL and LpxM to finally form Kdo-lipid A
expected_core_reactions.rationale: The paper asserts two sequential acylations, which entails a distinct LpxL step, but it names no intermediate between LpxL and LpxM.

expected_core_reactions.description: LpxM performs the second sequential acylation, finally forming Kdo-lipid A
substrates: singly acylated Kdo-lipid IVA intermediate (not named in this paper)
expected_core_reactions.quote: sequentially acylated by LpxL and LpxM to finally form Kdo-lipid A
expected_core_reactions.rationale: The paper asserts LpxM as the second of the two sequential acylations that completes Kdo-lipid A; its substrate is only implied by the word 'sequentially'.

expected_major_subprocesses.name: the Raetz pathway
expected_major_subprocesses.kind_rationale: The paper defines the Raetz pathway as 'a series of catalytic reactions' running from UDP-GlcNAc to Kdo-lipid A, so every member of the stage is a conversion of matter.
expected_major_subprocesses.quote: Kdo-lipid A is synthesized in the bacterial cytoplasm from a series of catalytic reactions that make up the Raetz pathway, named after Christian Raetz whose group pioneered the identification and characterization of the nine enzymes that make up the pathway
expected_major_subprocesses.rationale: The paper names the requested pathway as the Raetz pathway and enumerates its nine enzymes in catalytic order.

expected_major_subprocesses.name: early stages in the Raetz pathway
aliases: early steps of lipid A biosynthesis
expected_major_subprocesses.kind_rationale: The stage groups the LpxA acylation and the LpxC deacetylation, both substrate-to-product conversions; LpxC is simultaneously the pathway's regulated node, but the stage is a set of steps, so it is chemistry.
expected_major_subprocesses.quote: detergent-like LPS intermediates that accumulate upon hyperactivation of early stages in the Raetz pathway can be toxic, as depletion of the later-stage enzymes LpxH and LpxK resulted in growth defects that could be suppressed by inhibition of LpxA or LpxC
expected_major_subprocesses.rationale: The paper draws an explicit early/late division within the pathway and places LpxA and LpxC on the early side of it.

expected_major_subprocesses.name: later-stage Raetz pathway enzymes
aliases: late steps of lipid A biosynthesis
expected_major_subprocesses.kind_rationale: The paper groups LpxH and LpxK as the pathway's later-stage catalysts, and the two reactions it covers, UMP removal and phosphorylation to lipid IVA, are both chemical conversions.
expected_major_subprocesses.quote: depletion of the later-stage enzymes LpxH and LpxK resulted in growth defects
expected_major_subprocesses.rationale: The same sentence names LpxH and LpxK as the later-stage enzymes, so the paper itself groups them as a stage of the pathway.

expected_major_subprocesses.name: addition of the core sugars (Kdo transfer)
aliases: addition of the first sugar(s) of the core
expected_major_subprocesses.kind_rationale: Kdo residues are transferred onto lipid IVA to give Kdo-lipid IVA, an explicit substrate-to-product conversion.
expected_major_subprocesses.quote: The nine steps in the Raetz pathway as well as the subsequent addition of the core sugars are catalyzed in the cytoplasm or the cytoplasmic leaflet of the IM
expected_major_subprocesses.rationale: The paper treats core-sugar addition as a named stage adjoining the Raetz steps and includes WaaA in the Kdo-lipid A biosynthesis pathway of Figure 1B.

expected_major_subprocesses.name: sequential acylation of Kdo-lipid IVA by LpxL and LpxM
expected_major_subprocesses.kind_rationale: The stage is two successive acyl-transfer conversions of Kdo-lipid IVA that end at Kdo-lipid A.
expected_major_subprocesses.quote: resulting in Kdo-lipid IV A which is sequentially acylated by LpxL and LpxM to finally form Kdo-lipid A
expected_major_subprocesses.rationale: The paper explicitly groups the two terminal acylations as one sequential stage that completes Kdo-lipid A.

important_participants.note: Rendered in the source as 'lipid IV A', with a space before the roman numeral subscript.

important_participants.name: Kdo
important_participants.quote: the first sugar(s) of the core, 3-deoxy-D- manno -oct-2-ulosonic acid (Kdo)

uncertainties: The paper delivers the entire chemistry of the requested pathway in ONE paragraph plus the Figure 1 legend. Roughly 85% of the body is about LpxC regulation, and much of that is in organisms other than the requested E. coli.

R3 (LpxD), R4 (LpxH/I/G), R8 (LpxL) and R9 (LpxM) have NO chemically named substrate or product in this paper; the transformation type and the catalyst are asserted but the species are only positional ('the next acyl group', 'sequentially acylated'). They are recorded as core because the paper asserts the transformations, but at medium confidence; a reviewer may prefer to treat them as enzyme assertions rather than as reactions.

The LpxA product and the LpxC product are never chemically named for E. coli in the body. The only chemically named LpxC product in the paper, 'UDP-3-O-(R-3-hydroxydecanoyl)-glucosamine', is explicitly the P. aeruginosa product and must not be attached to the E. coli chain. The E. coli LpxA product IS named inside a REFERENCE TITLE in the bibliography (reference 7), but that is a cited work's title, not an assertion of this paper's body, so I did not use it.

R8 and R9 could legitimately be curated as a SINGLE reaction ('Kdo-lipid IVA is sequentially acylated by LpxL and LpxM to form Kdo-lipid A'). I split them because the paper says the acylations are sequential and counts nine enzymes; a reviewer preferring one entry would not be wrong.

The sentence 'The nine steps in the Raetz pathway as well as the subsequent addition of the core sugars' can be read as EXCLUDING WaaA from the nine. Counting the enzymes the paper lists in order (LpxA, LpxC, LpxD, LpxH/I/G, LpxB, LpxK, WaaA, LpxL, LpxM) gives exactly nine only if WaaA is included. I included it; this is a genuine internal ambiguity in the source.
LpxH, LpxI and LpxG are given as organism-dependent alternatives in R4. The paper does not state which one E. coli uses. R4 lists all three; that is not an assertion that E. coli has three.
beta-hydroxyacyl-ACP is important in R1 but is also treated elsewhere in the paper as a shared FAS II currency species competed for by FabZ. It is recorded as important only for R1.

The regulators FtsH, LapB, YejM and ObgE are recorded as SECONDARY with reaction_ids pointing at the reaction whose CATALYST they control. They participate in no lipid A chemistry. If the downstream consumer expects secondary participants to be chemical species only, these four should be filtered out.

I deliberately did NOT record 'regulation of LpxC' or the 'YejM-LapB-FtsH partner switching' module as a major subprocess, even though it is the bulk of the paper. It is a regulatory module governing flux, not a constituent chemical stage of the requested pathway. The pinned gold case is consistent: it lists FtsH, LapB and YejM as acceptable_enzymes, not expected_enzymes.
No disagreement found between the pinned gold case and the paper.
